title: JUACO: a minimal artificial organism evolved under a preregistered, replicated and audited research protocol run by LLM agents
description:
JUACO is an artificial-life research project. Minimal digital organisms follow local rules, with no backpropagation, and live, eat, reproduce and evolve in simulated worlds. The project asks how far natural selection can go at building capabilities that nobody designed.

It is also an experiment in method. One researcher directs a team of LLM agents under a strict protocol: preregistration before any data, bit-for-bit identity harnesses, controls that can fail, replication on new seeds, and an independent audit that recomputes numbers from raw files. Every error is numbered and kept (ERR-1 to ERR-153).

Verified results (closed and replicated) are listed in RESULTADOS_VERIFICADOS.md. Among them: given composable rule blocks, natural selection alone assembles and duplicates a heritable rejection rule that sustains lineages without a nursery (19/20 seeds, twice). The author reproduced this result bit-for-bit on his own machine.
